images.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this photographic editorial illustration so that its physical connection also explains a software relationship: an agent connects through an MCP server to the Google Ads API. Preserve the beautiful macro framing, cobalt braided cable, yellow enclosure, machined metal, exposed internal copper/circuit board, mineral table and directional lighting. Landscape 1536x1024.
Add just three exceptionally legible physical labels, integrated into the objects with correct material and perspective:
1. A neat small ivory cable identification sleeve on the blue cable near its lower-left visible portion, printed "Agent" in graphite sans-serif.
2. On the smooth silver collar immediately before the knurled middle, engrave and dark-infill "MCP".
3. On the broad yellow front enclosure panel, print "Google Ads API" in dark charcoal industrial sans-serif, sized prominently enough to read at article width.
The cable, connector, and enclosure MUST make this ordering unambiguous; each label belongs to its own physical part. Reposition only enough to show labels clearly. No floating callouts, no headline, no diagram arrows or boxes, no extra captions or acronyms, no fake logo, no data/results. This remains a sophisticated tactile conceptual photograph. Clear print, exact spelling, no illegible filler lettering. Do not label copper components.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Turn this elegant photographic still life into a USEFUL editorial explanation of a Monday reporting workflow, while preserving the loupe, translucent paper, sparse cobalt ink, single yellow clip, mineral tabletop, macro realism, directional light and landscape 1536x1024. Recompose the papers and loupe slightly as needed for very legible sparse lettering.
Remove the meaningless abstract bars/grid marks. Instead arrange TWO distinct translucent source strips feeding under ONE central ivory report sheet, separated enough that their physical labels are readable: one source strip from left printed "Google Ads" with a smaller "Accounts"; a second source strip from upper right printed "CRM". The main report sheet is printed in refined clear graphite sans-serif: "Monday report" at top; a smaller organizing line "Offer / Campaign type"; then four generous field labels laid out in a spare 2-by-2 arrangement: "Spend", "Revenue", "Conversions", "ROAS". A small footer line on this paper reads "7-day / 30-day change". All text must be on actual paper surfaces with correct perspective. No other text.
The loupe lies toward lower-right, bringing one or two of the field names into enlarged focus but not obscuring/warping them beyond recognition. Leave the other labels fully readable. Do not fill this with a data table. No business numbers, no invented values, no claims or charts. This is an imagined physical report layout illustrating sources, grouping and measures, NOT actual account performance.
Keep expressive angled layering, exquisite glass caustics and translucent material detail. The point is two named data sources become one report organized for the reader, with only these few useful labels. NOT a flat infographic, stock office scene, dashboard screenshot or slide.
